QuestionStmt.S: Identify the reagent $R$ used in following reaction. $$\text{Ketone} \xrightarrow{R} \text{semicarbazone}$$

Solution.S:
Semicarbazone is formed when a ketone (or aldehyde) reacts with semicarbazide. Semicarbazide has the formula $\mathrm{NH_2-NH-CONH_2}$ or $\mathrm{NH_2NHCONH_2}$.

Option A ($\mathrm{NH_2OH}$) is hydroxylamine → forms oxime.
Option B ($\mathrm{NH_2NHCONH_2}$) is semicarbazide → forms semicarbazone.
Option C ($\mathrm{NH_2NHC_6H_5}$) is phenylhydrazine → forms phenylhydrazone.
Option D ($\mathrm{NH_2NH_2}$) is hydrazine → forms hydrazone.

Thus, the correct reagent is semicarbazide, which is option B.
